source_files.role: The oracle. 652 lines, 15 START_SECTIONs, all ported. Every transcribed literal in tests/mzxml.rs comes from here.

Not ported here. Read for the attribute and conversion helpers the handler relies on: attributeAsString_/attributeAsInt_/attributeAsDouble_ are fatal when absent, the optionalAttributeAs*_ char16_t overloads assign before returning and the String one returns !value.empty(), asDouble_/asInt_ log a non-fatal error and return zero, and asDateTime_ trims to 19 characters and logs instead of failing.
Not ported here. Read for cvStringToEnum_ (first match wins, unknown term warns and returns index 0) and for error/warning being log-only while fatalError throws.

Not ported here. The base class MzXMLFile inherits: schema_location_/schema_version_, getVersion, isValid (unported, needs the mzXML XSD) and the compression-sniffing parse_/save_ pair this crate's path_io replaces.

fixtures.role: Unmodified upstream. The package's main fixture: four scans with MS levels 1/1/1/2 where scan 13 is an XML child of scan 12, 32-bit big-endian peak pairs, two <parentFile> records, a full <msInstrument> with an <operator> and two <nameValue> entries, two <dataProcessing> steps, three <precursorMz> elements and a scan <comment>. It declares pairOrder= rather than contentType=, an attribute the handler never reads, and declares the mzXML_2.1 namespace while OpenMS registers 3.1.
Unmodified upstream. MzXMLFile_1 with compressionType="zlib" on every <peaks>; MzXMLFile_test.cpp:343-348 asserts the two load to equal experiments.

Unmodified upstream. One scan whose base64 is broken by spaces, a newline and a tab, an empty fileSha1, and no retentionTime attribute, which the source reads as 0.0 rather than the MSSpectrum sentinel -1.

Unmodified upstream. Mixes precision="32" and precision="64" payloads, exercises the composite durations PT1S / PT2M1S / PT1H61S (1, 121 and 3661 seconds), all three polarity spellings any/+/-, scanType Full and zoom, and startMz/endMz. Its first payload ends AA1=, whose two surplus base64 bits are set: a canonical decoder refuses it, and MzXMLFile_test.cpp:313 asserts the resulting intensity 100.0000991821289.

Hand-written for this package; not upstream. A three-level scan tree (MS1 > MS2 > MS3) in which every level carries a <nameValue> and a <comment> AFTER its nested child, which is the shape that reveals the upstream metadata misattribution, plus a fourth scan whose <peaks> is xsi:nil. Peak payloads are (120,100), (121,50) and (122,25) as 32-bit big-endian pairs.

NOT copied into this repository: 10.6 MB would more than double tests/data, whose current largest entry is 3.4 MB. Hashed here for provenance. It is one scan with peaksCount="997530" and retentionTime="-PT1S", written by OpenMS itself for a spectrum whose retention time was the MSSpectrum default -1. tests/mzxml.rs generates an equivalent document with the same 997530 peaks and asserts the upstream count; the coordinates are independently derived.

source_anchors.operation: the constructor registers /SCHEMAS/mzXML_idx_3.1.xsd and version 3.1, which is the only place the schema version is set
the transform overload that takes a map forces setAlwaysAppendData(true) on a copy of the options, so the caller's false does not suppress the map

transformFirstPass_ sets metadata_only = skip_full_count AND load_detail = LD_RAWCOUNTS; with skip_full_count true the scan handler throws EndParsingSoftly before ++scan_count_, so the consumer is told to expect zero spectra
if (skip_spectrum_ && tag != "scan") return — a filtered scan swallows every child except a nested <scan>, and the nested scan resets the flag
the <peaks> handler indexes spectrum_data_.back() unconditionally; with no open <scan> the vector is empty and this is undefined behaviour

an unknown precision, a non-network byteOrder, a non-m/z-int contentType and an unknown compressionType are reported through error(LOAD, ...), which only writes to the log stream; decoding then proceeds with the wrong interpretation
the pair order is read from contentType, not from the pairOrder attribute MzXMLFile_1.mzXML actually writes, so the default m/z-int carries that fixture
precursorIntensity is read with the throwing attributeAsDouble_ inside a try/catch that logs and leaves the intensity at its default zero

windowWideness is stored whole in the lower isolation offset and halved into both offsets only when the m/z character content arrives, so an empty <precursorMz/> keeps the full width in the lower offset
metadata_only throws EndParsingSoftly on the first <scan>, after nesting_level_++ and before ++scan_count_
xs:duration parsing takes StringUtils::suffix(time_string, 'T'), which discards the leading sign and any day component, then adds the H, M and S components; -PT1S therefore reads as +1
++scan_count_ happens before the RT/MS-level/LD_RAWCOUNTS filter, so getScanCount() counts every scan in the file
spectrum.reserve(peak_count_ / 2 + 1) reserves half of what the decode loop needs; the comment above it ("peak count == twice the scan size") contradicts the loop at :1177 and is stale
a ScanWindow is stored only when startMz or endMz is nonzero, and neither is compared against the other
scanType EPI rewrites the MS level to 2, and ER and zoom set the zoom-scan flag; EMS, EPI and ER are non-standard ABI Sashimi values
<msResolution> indexes getMassAnalyzers()[0] unconditionally, which is undefined behaviour when it precedes <msMassAnalyzer>
<nameValue> and <software> read *(open_tags_.end() - 2) for the parent tag, which is out of bounds when the element is the document root

a <nameValue> inside a <scan> is attached to spectrum_data_.back(), the most recently STARTED scan; nothing pops that on </scan>, so a parent's nameValue written after a nested child lands on the child
the pending batch is flushed only when nesting_level_ reaches zero, so an entire nested scan tree is committed together
onCharacters applies setMZ and the window halving per text chunk, so a split <precursorMz> halves the window twice; setComment at :605 likewise keeps only the last chunk of a split comment
a precursor m/z outside the configured range sets skip_spectrum_ and pops spectrum_data_, which for a nested scan can pop a different spectrum than the one being filtered
writeTo counts only nonempty spectra for scanCount and bumps a zero to one, because an empty mzXML is not schema-valid
msRun startTime and endTime are the FIRST and LAST spectrum's retention times, not the minimum and maximum, and no sign is written, so a default -1 becomes the invalid PT-1S
fileType is an mzXML enumeration, so the OpenMS free-text type is lowercased and searched for "raw"; a checksum that is not 40 SHA-1 characters is replaced with forty zeros at :674
an empty vendor plus an acquisition software name containing "xcalibur" makes the writer claim "Thermo Scientific", because MaxQuant's parameter defaults require it
<msResolution> is omitted when the resolution method has no mzXML name, but must not be empty when written, or MaxQuant crashes on loading
the data processing of the FIRST spectrum is written as the whole file's <dataProcessing>; other spectra's processing is discarded

native IDs are classified before writing: all bare numbers or all scan=-prefixed numbers are preserved, anything else is renumbered from one, and the loss is only warned about when at least one nonempty ID was unparsable
force_mq_compatibility skips empty spectra with continue, but the next MS level at :1086 is still read from cexp_[s+1] even when that spectrum is about to be skipped
indentation is std::string(ms_level + 1, '\t'), so a hostile MS level allocates gigabytes of tabs per written line
under force_mq_compatibility an unsorted spectrum is reported through error(STORE, ...), which only logs, and begin()->getMZ() and rbegin()->getMZ() are written as lowMz and highMz regardless
basePeakMz is the one statistics attribute written unconditionally; lowMz, highMz, basePeakIntensity and totIonCurrent need force_mq_compatibility
precursorIntensity is written as (int)precursor.getIntensity(), truncating a fractional intensity
the precursor m/z written is the acquisition's [Thermo Trailer Extra]Monoisotopic M/Z: meta value when present, because the old ReAdW converter uses it and it is more accurate

the <peaks> tag is broken across lines under force_mq_compatibility because MaxQuant's reader fails otherwise, while TPP tools such as SpectraST cannot deal with the breaks; a fatalError guards against the newlines being removed by a later edit
the writer always emits precision="32", byteOrder="network", contentType="m/z-int", compressionType="none" and compressedLen="0", narrowing every f64 m/z to float
an empty spectrum writes <peaks ... xsi:nil="true" /> with no payload
the scan nesting is derived from MS levels alone: when the next level is not higher, ms_level - next_ms_level + 1 scans are closed, stopping early if the open-scan stack empties
the <index>/<indexOffset> trailer is written when write_index OR force_mq_compatibility is set, with spaces around the = of the index and offset attributes
writeUserParam_ skips only keys whose first character is '#', and does not skip the keys already written as <scan> attributes, so filterLine and the statistics keys are emitted twice
doPopulateSpectraWithData_ returns immediately for an empty char_rest_, so a nonzero peaksCount with an empty payload is not an error

assert(data.size() == 2 * spectrum_data.peak_count_) is compiled out in release builds and the loop then runs to 2 * peak_count_ reading data[n] and data[n+1], so a short payload reads past the decoded buffer; the 32-bit branch at :1202 is identical
populateSpectraWithData_ decodes the pending batch under #pragma omp parallel for, counts failures in an atomic and re-throws one ParseError for any of them

init_ builds the five position-indexed CV tables; cv_terms_[1] is documented as no longer used, and the ionization, analyzer, detector and resolution tables are padded to their enum sizes with empty strings that cvStringToEnum_ never reaches because index 0 is also empty
cvStringToEnum_ returns the FIRST matching table index and, for an unknown term, warns and returns result_on_error, which defaults to zero
error() and warning() only write to the log stream; only fatalError() throws, so every error(LOAD, ...) in MzXMLHandler is a load that continues
asDateTime_ trims the string to its first 19 BYTES with StringUtils::substr before parsing, which would split a multi-byte character
the char16_t optionalAttributeAsString_ overload returns !value.empty(), so a present but empty attribute assigns the empty string and still reports false
DRange::encloses is closed below and OPEN above (position >= max_ returns false), so every PeakFileOptions range excludes its own maximum

evidence: Tier 3 source review. Expectations are transcribed C++ literals from MzXMLFile_test.cpp (652 lines, 15 START_SECTIONs, all ported, none merely mapped) and the four unmodified upstream fixtures listed above: four scans with MS levels 1/1/1/2 and sizes 1/3/5/5, native IDs scan=10..scan=13, peak coordinates 100..140 with intensities 100..300, the two parentFile records with SHA-1 digests 2fd4e1c67a2d28fced849ee1bb76e7391b93eb12 and ...eb13, the MS-X 1.0 / MS-Y 1.1 processing steps with the 2001-02-03 04:05:06 completion time and the 3.4 intensity cutoff, the MS-Vendor / MS 1 / ESI / Quadrupole Ion Trap / Faraday Cup / FWHM / MS-Z 3.0 instrument, the FirstName/LastName/0049/a@b.de/http://bla.de operator, the three precursors at m/z 101/201/301 with intensities 100/200/300, charges 1/2/3 and half-widths 5/10/15, the 64-bit fixture's retention times 1/121/3661 from PT1S/PT2M1S/PT1H61S and its 100.0000991821289 intensity from a non-canonical base64 tail, the 997530-peak long spectrum, and the total ion current 2300 over 14 peaks that both transform sections assert. TRANSCRIBED C++ LITERALS ARE TIER-3 EVIDENCE: they detect transcription drift, not a misread algorithm. No C++ was built or executed, no C++ output was retained, and there is no oracle driver, so this is NOT a tier 1 differential. Independent of that suite: the store/load round trip of MzXMLFile_1.mzXML is asserted field by field on the whole MSExperiment rather than on selected values, and the written <index> offsets are dereferenced back into the document and required to land exactly on their <scan num="N"> tags, which no OpenMS read path checks. The resource ceilings, the four attribute rejections, the peaksCount/payload comparison, the nested-scan metadata attribution, the retention-time sign, the writer's lossless defaults, the non-ASCII inputs and the eleven malformed documents are tier 4, independently derived, because no upstream fixture reaches them.
gaps: XMLFile::isValid against mzXML_idx_3.1.xsd is not ported: this crate embeds no mzXML schema and crate::format::mzml_schema is mzML-only. The one assertion of the upstream [EXTRA] isValid section is replaced by a structural check (3.1 namespace and schema location present, balanced <scan> elements, reloads to the same experiment), which is weaker than XSD validation and is labelled as such in docs/MZXML_SUPPORT.md.

ProgressLogger is a constructor parameter of both source classes and is not threaded through this module; there is no progress callback. The non-fatal observations the source sends to its log stream come back in ReadReport instead.
src/format/file_handler.rs does not dispatch FileType::MzXml to this module, although the file type and its content magic already exist. That file is outside this package.
The source parallelises batch decoding with #pragma omp parallel for (MzXMLHandler.cpp:1224); this port is serial, so a large file decodes on one core.

docs/doc-coverage.json was not rewritten: src/format/mzxml.rs measures 100.0% (42/42) and check_doc_coverage.py reports an improvement, but recording the new floor with --write touches a file outside this package's scope.

docs/core-sdk-coverage.json and docs/CORE_SDK_COMPLETION.md are stale because the coverage script now detects src/format/mzxml.rs as a candidate file for FORMAT/MzXMLFile.h. Regenerating them with python3 tools/core_sdk_coverage.py --write, after the two ledger entries are added, is the integrating agent's step; both files are outside this package.

CI wiring was not added: append '--test mzxml' to a '--no-default-features --features mzml' line of the minimum-rust job in .github/workflows/rust.yml (rust.yml:86 or :87). The test passes under --features mzml alone and under cargo +1.85.0.

MzXMLFile_4_long.mzXML is not copied (10.6 MB); the long-spectrum section is reproduced from a generated document with the same peak count. The upstream file's sha256 is recorded above, so it can be added later without ambiguity.

mzXML cannot express the sample description, the HPLC gradient, instrument configurations, more than one ion source or analyzer, chromatograms, auxiliary data arrays, ion mobility or peptide identifications. Storing an mzML-derived experiment drops them, as upstream does; this is a format limit, not a port limit.
